Q: node.js tracing on performance api produces no events A:

It seems that the functionality has been removed:

This does remove the user timing and timerify trace events. Because the trace_events are still considered experimental, those can be removed without a deprecation cycle. They are removed to improve performance and reduce complexity.

Q: Print results of multi-lined substitutions only A:

Ah, I should have tested that. The * quantifier can sometimes give unexpected results. Apparently, .*? controls where the match ends, but it still starts as early as possible. In either case, your best bet is to use string capture to catch what you need, and not substitution to trim away everything you don't need.

As for your question on ikegami's answer, this is not a regular question, so it does not have an accept button. Was there something about my solution that you thought was wrong? It is virtually identical to ikegami's.

If the -g switch doesn't work for you, you are probably using a Perl version less than v5.36.

Q: Recoding in R without typing the original variable values? A:

You can also use the .GRP special in data.table:

library(data.table)
setDT(example_df)[, let(id2=.GRP), id]

Q: VBA Pivot Freezing Sheet A:

Here's another take: see comments for any explanations.

Pivot table for counting was replaced by use of Scripting.Dictionary to count as we go through the data...

Option Explicit

Sub CountItems()
    
    Const RW_START_DISCREP As Long = 2 'first row for discrepancies
    Dim ws As Worksheet, r As Long, LastRow As Long, rngData As Range, data As Variant
    Dim hadDiscrepancy As Boolean, rwDiscrep As Range
    Dim dictBCount As Object, dictFcount As Object, k
    
    
    Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Data") 'if sheet in same wb as this code
    LastRow = GetLastRow(ws, "B", "F") 'Check cols B/2 and F/6 for last row with data
                                       '    This makes the loop below much simpler
    
    Set rngData = ws.Range("A2:F" & LastRow)    'the range with data
    data = rngData.Value                        'read all the data into a 2D array
    
    Set rwDiscrep = ws.Cells(RW_START_DISCREP, "L").Resize(1, 3) 'first discrepancy output range
    
    Set dictBCount = GetDict() 'Create a couple of dictionaries for counting unique
    Set dictFcount = GetDict() '   items in columns B and F
    
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    
    'loop over the data (much faster than looping over the range)
    For r = 1 To UBound(data, 1)
        'Replace ColF cell that says Mix|Mixed with either a blank cell or the same item as ColB
        If data(r, 6) = "MIX" Or data(r, 6) = "MIXED" Then
            
            With rngData.Cells(r, 6) 'update the sheet
                If data(r, 2) = "" Then
                    .Value = ""
                    .Interior.Color = vbRed
                Else
                    .Value = data(r, 2)
                End If
            End With
            
        'Check to see if the item numbers match and the palletIDs match
        '### Note this comment from the OP does not follow the logic below ###
        ElseIf data(r, 2) <> data(r, 6) And data(r, 1) = data(r, 5) Then
            rwDiscrep.Value = Array(data(r, 1), data(r, 2), data(r, 6))
            Set rwDiscrep = rwDiscrep.Offset(1) 'next row for discrepancy
            hadDiscrepancy = True 'set flag
        End If
        
        'Increment unique value counts for cols B and F
        k = CStr(data(r, 2))
        If Len(k) > 0 Then dictBCount(k) = dictBCount(k) + 1
        k = CStr(data(r, 6))
        If Len(k) > 0 Then dictFcount(k) = dictFcount(k) + 1
        
    Next r
    'if no discrepancies, flag that on the sheet
    If Not hadDiscrepancy Then rwDiscrep.Cells(1).Value = "No Discrepancies"
    
    'Finally put the unique values and counts on the worksheet
    DumpDictionary ws.Range("P2"), dictBCount, "Col B Values", "ValueCount"
    DumpDictionary ws.Range("S2"), dictFcount, "Col F Values", "ValueCount"
End Sub

'### Everything below here is re-usable....

'Utility method: find the last row with data in any column(s) passed to `CheckCols`
Function GetLastRow(ws As Worksheet, ParamArray CheckCols()) As Long
    Dim lr As Long, maxRow As Long, col
    For Each col In CheckCols
        lr = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, col).End(xlUp).Row
        If lr > maxRow Then maxRow = lr
    Next col
    GetLastRow = maxRow
End Function

'Create and return a case-insensitive dictionary
Function GetDict() As Object 'Scripting.Dictionary
    Dim rv As Object
    Set rv = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
    rv.CompareMode = 1 'vbTextCompare: case-insensitive
    Set GetDict = rv
End Function

'Given a Dictionary `dict`, compile its contents into an array and place the
'  array on a worksheet starting at `rngTopLeft`, using the supplied column headers
Sub DumpDictionary(rngTopLeft As Range, dict As Object, KeysHeader As String, ValuesHeader As String)
    Dim data, k, r As Long, ubr As Long
    ubr = dict.Count + 1
    ReDim data(1 To ubr, 1 To 2) 'size the output array
    data(1, 1) = KeysHeader      'add the headers
    data(1, 2) = ValuesHeader
    r = 2
    For Each k In dict           'add keys and values
        data(r, 1) = k
        data(r, 2) = dict(k)
        r = r + 1
    Next k
    rngTopLeft.Resize(ubr, 2).Value = data 'put the data on the worksheet starting at `rngTopLeft`
End Sub
